before.statement_or_definition: Show the projective Clifford+T one-qubit subgroup is dense: normalize \(H,T\) into \(h=iH\in SU(2)\) and \(t=e^{-i\pi/8}T\in SU(2)\), take \(V=ht\), and compute \(\operatorname{tr}V=\sqrt2\sin(\pi/8)=x\). The minimal polynomial of x is \(2X^4-4X^2+1\), not monic; prove its degree is four using the norm of \(x^2=1-\sqrt2/2\). Thus x is not an algebraic integer. If an eigenangle of V were rational in units of \(\pi\), the trace would be a sum of roots of unity and hence an algebraic integer, contradiction. Powers of V are dense on one SU(2) torus; conjugation by t gives a nonparallel axis; an explicit two-axis Euler/coordinate lemma yields all SU(2). The normalized matrices are SU(2) lifts of raw H/T labels; translating the resulting word back to raw labels preserves only the projective class unless its scalar is tracked.
proof_obligations: Root algebraic-integer minimal-polynomial criterion, ring-of-integers/cyclotomic field and root-of-unity facts; local irrational-rotation and two-axis Euler lemmas. The gate normalization phases are tracked, not deleted under a control.

after.statement_or_definition: For a unitary partitioned into equal square blocks, there exist block-diagonal unitaries L=diag(L0,L1), R=diag(R0,R1) and real diagonal C,S with C²+S²=I, 0≤C,S≤I, such that U=L[[C,−S],[S,C]]R. Zero and unit singular values are permitted.
proof_obligations: Apply SVD to the upper-left block. Column orthogonality identifies the Gram matrices of the lower-left and upper-right blocks as I−C²; choose their singular bases compatibly on positive singular supports.

Use row orthogonality on the shared positive supports to identify the lower-right block; complete bases in the zero/unit singular sectors to arrange its residual unitary. Verify all four blocks and C²+S²=I, including degenerate sectors. This is the exact finite matrix route; numerical angle extraction is separate.

proof_obligations: Parameterize one-qubit gates by SU(2) Euler charts plus one aggregate scalar. Immediately before each CNOT, a Z rotation on the control and an X rotation on the target commute through that CNOT and can be absorbed into the preceding local layer. These are two independent one-dimensional stabilizer directions out of the six local parameters on that pair, leaving at most four new parameters.

Iterate this absorption to obtain finitely/countably many smooth parameter charts of dimension ≤3n+4m+1. Sard applied in local U(2^n) charts makes every lower-dimensional image measure zero; finite CNOT skeletons and countable charts preserve measure zero. Prove the unitary-group chart dimension 4^n via skew-Hermitian tangent coordinates and a local Cayley transform.

Stabilizer exact simulator
after.statement_or_definition: Input n-bit basis state and finite adaptive H,S,S†,CNOT/Pauli-measurement instruction list with an explicit finite classical-control program and fair-bit sampler. Store n independent signed Pauli generators initially (−1)^x_j Z_j. For each gate conjugate every row with the exact Pauli product/conjugation formulas. To measure Hermitian M, find the first anticommuting row g. If found, choose fair b, multiply every other anticommuting row by g, replace g by (−1)^b M, and record b. Otherwise solve the n-row binary membership system by leftmost-pivot Gaussian elimination, multiply the selected signed rows in fixed order and compare their sign to M to obtain deterministic b. Evaluate classical control on the existing transcript, continue, and return transcript plus final rows. Invalid non-Hermitian measurements or unavailable gates return INVALID.
proof_obligations: Every instruction and elimination has a bounded finite loop. Prove signed-row invariant, measurement law and polynomial bit cost in the existing Gottesman–Knill theorem; fair-bit randomness is the only sampling primitive.

after.statement_or_definition: Input r independent commuting signed Hermitian Pauli rows excluding −I on n wires, r≤n. For pivot j=0,...,r−1: take first remaining nonidentity row, choose first nonzero unused wire and SWAP it to j. On each unused wire convert that row local X to Z with H, Y to Z with chronological S† then H, leaving Z fixed; conjugate every row with each gate. For every remaining Z at wire k≠j apply CNOT(k→j), again updating all rows, leaving the pivot as ±Z_j. If its sign is minus, apply X_j. Commuting remaining rows have no X_j; multiply each with Z_j bit 1 by the pivot to clear it. Continue on unused wires. Record gates D sending input checks to +Z_0,...,+Z_(r−1); output D† as encoder acting on |0^r> tensor logical basis |x>, together with each signed row-operation map and that logical basis convention. Invalid dependent/noncommuting/−I inputs return INVALID.
proof_obligations: Give a terminating row/column elimination algorithm with exact H/S/CNOT/SWAP updates and phase tracking.
For every branch, preserve commutation and row-space invariants; bound gate count and workspace.

after.statement_or_definition: For integer d≥2 take the square grid with vertices (i,j), 0≤i,j≤d and unit horizontal/vertical edges. Let R be the left and right vertical boundaries, including their vertices and edges. Use relative F2 chain spaces C2(all d² faces), C1(edges not in R; 2d² qubits), C0(vertices not in R). Order coordinates lexicographically. Z checks are boundaries of faces with R edges deleted; X checks are rows of the relative incidence C1→C0. Missing face/outside dual boundaries are the top and bottom; left/right are rough. Define the code by these commuting checks, without physical/topological-order premises.
proof_obligations: The relative incidence of each face boundary is zero because each nonrough vertex occurs twice; hence every X/Z check pair commutes.
Explicit check matrices, boundary identification, and chosen primal/dual strings are part of the definition. Chain/homology assertions are proved in the next theorem.

before.title: QC20 Square Planar Surface Code Distance And Path Count

after.statement_or_definition: For this relative d×d square patch, there is one logical qubit, distance d, and each Z logical crossing has length at least d. Primal self-avoiding rough-to-rough paths of length ell are bounded by (d+1)3^ell (there are d+1 left starting edges and at most three later continuations). Dual top-to-bottom logical crossings have minimum length d+1, so both types have weight at least d.
proof_obligations: Relative vertex incidence has rank (d−1)(d+1)=d²−1: any nonrough vertex subset with zero coboundary is empty by connectivity to a rough edge. Relative face boundary has rank d²: peeling the topmost face of a nonzero 2-chain detects an undeleted horizontal edge. Thus k=2d²−(d²−1)−d²=1.

A relative cycle decomposes into closed loops and rough-to-rough paths. Same-side paths/loops bound relative face chains; a left-to-right path is the unique nontrivial class and requires d horizontal steps. A straight horizontal row attains d. Duality by the explicit check matrix gives top-to-bottom paths crossing d+1 horizontal-edge rows; no smaller nontrivial dual class exists.
Count left start heights j=0,...,d and choose at most three next edges when immediate backtracking is excluded. Logical failures can be reduced to self-avoiding paths by deleting loops.
